## Highlights

A data-safety release. In earlier versions, opening a note and making any edit could rewrite parts of it you never touched. Upgrading is recommended, especially on Windows.

## Fixes

- **CRLF notes are no longer double-spaced.** Notes saved with Windows line endings had every line doubled on the first autosave. The editor now works in LF and saves CRLF notes with CRLF. A note that mixes line endings is saved with CRLF throughout.
- **Long CRLF notes are no longer truncated.** The 10,000-line limit now counts lines the way the editor holds them, at startup and when restoring from trash. Before, a CRLF note could pass the check and then be cut short.
- **Tabs are kept.** Tabs in notes and pastes used to be replaced by four spaces. They now stay as tabs and are drawn four cells wide.
- **U+FFFD is kept.** A literal replacement character (`�`) in a note or paste is no longer deleted.
- **Notes with control characters are left alone.** Notes containing control characters other than tabs and line endings (for example form feed) are skipped at startup with a warning naming them, instead of being saved without those characters. Restoring such a note from trash is refused the same way.
- **Empty Linux clipboard.** Ctrl+V with an empty clipboard now says "Clipboard is empty" instead of reporting a `wl-paste`/`xclip` failure.

## Downloads and validation

Archives are available for **Linux and Windows**, on **amd64 and arm64**, with `SHA256SUMS`.

New regression tests check that editing and saving a note keeps LF, CRLF, mixed, tab and U+FFFD content byte for byte. They also cover tab-aware wrapping and cursor movement, control-character handling at load, restore and paste, and empty-clipboard detection.
